questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three recognized methods of architect selection under the SPP?

options.text: Direct Selection by Owner
Comparative Selection (Shortlisting)
Architectural Design Competition (ADC)
Lowest Bidder Selection

rationale.a: Direct Selection by Owner is incorrect as an answer because it IS one of the three recognized methods. The Owner directly engages an architect of their choice.
rationale.b: Comparative Selection (Shortlisting) is incorrect as an answer because it IS one of the three recognized methods. Multiple architects are evaluated and compared.
rationale.c: Architectural Design Competition (ADC) is incorrect as an answer because it IS one of the three recognized methods, governed by SPP 208.
rationale.d: Lowest Bidder Selection is correct. The SPP explicitly does NOT recognize lowest-bid selection for architectural services, as professional services are not commodities subject to price-based bidding.
rationale.correct: The three recognized methods of architect selection under SPP are: (1) Direct Selection, (2) Comparative Selection/Shortlisting, and (3) Architectural Design Competition. Lowest bidder selection is prohibited for professional architectural services.
rationale.takeaway: Architectural services use Direct, Comparative, or ADC selection — never lowest-bid.

questions.explanation: The three recognized methods of architect selection under SPP are: (1) Direct Selection, (2) Comparative Selection/Shortlisting, and (3) Architectural Design Competition. Lowest bidder selection is prohibited for professional architectural services.

questions.text: What does the acronym IAPOA stand for in the context of Philippine architectural practice?

options.text: International Association of Professional Organizations of Architects
Integrated Accredited Professional Organization of Architects
Institute of Architectural Practitioners and Organizations Association
International Architects and Planners Organization of Asia

rationale.a: This is incorrect. IAPOA is a national, not international, organization.
rationale.b: Correct. IAPOA stands for the Integrated Accredited Professional Organization of Architects, which is the UAP's formal designation under R.A. 9266.
rationale.c: This is a fabricated name and does not match IAPOA's actual meaning.
rationale.d: This is incorrect. IAPOA is specific to Philippine practice, not an Asia-wide body.
rationale.correct: IAPOA stands for Integrated Accredited Professional Organization of Architects. Under R.A. 9266, the UAP serves as the IAPOA — the sole accredited professional organization for architects in the Philippines, responsible for professional standards and advocacy.
rationale.takeaway: IAPOA = Integrated Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (i.e., the UAP).

questions.explanation: IAPOA stands for Integrated Accredited Professional Organization of Architects. Under R.A. 9266, the UAP serves as the IAPOA — the sole accredited professional organization for architects in the Philippines, responsible for professional standards and advocacy.

questions.text: When did the 2010 UAP Standards of Professional Practice (SPP) take effect?

options.text: January 1, 2010
March 9, 2011
December 31, 2011

rationale.a: January 1, 2010 is incorrect. While the SPP was adopted in 2010, its effectivity date was tied to the PRC approval, not the calendar year start.
rationale.b: March 9, 2011 is correct. The SPP took effect upon PRC-Board of Architecture Resolution approval on this date, as documented in the UAP SPP overview.
rationale.c: June 15, 2010 is incorrect. This date has no significance in the SPP approval timeline.
rationale.d: December 31, 2011 is incorrect. The SPP was already in effect well before the end of 2011.
rationale.correct: The 2010 UAP Standards of Professional Practice took effect on March 9, 2011, upon approval by the PRC-Board of Architecture through a formal Resolution. This is the legal basis under R.A. 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004).
rationale.takeaway: The SPP effective date is March 9, 2011 — not the year of adoption (2010).

questions.explanation: The 2010 UAP Standards of Professional Practice took effect on March 9, 2011, upon approval by the PRC-Board of Architecture through a formal Resolution. This is the legal basis under R.A. 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004).

questions.text: Annex 'A' of the 2010 SPP series replaces which previous UAP document?

options.text: UAP Doc. 201
UAP Doc. 206
UAP Doc. 208
UAP Doc. 209

rationale.a: UAP Doc. 201 is incorrect. The previous Doc. 201 was replaced by the new SPP Doc. 201, not by Annex A.
rationale.b: UAP Doc. 206 is incorrect. Doc. 206 was replaced by the new SPP Doc. 206.
rationale.c: Correct. Annex 'A' (Interior Design Fee Schedule) replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 208, which previously covered interior design fees.
rationale.d: UAP Doc. 209 is incorrect. The 1979 Doc. 209 was replaced by SPP Doc. 208 (Architectural Design Competition), not by Annex A.
rationale.correct: Annex 'A' of the 2010 SPP, which covers the Interior Design Fee Schedule, replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 208. This is a commonly tested distinction because the numbering shifted between the 1979 and 2010 series.
rationale.takeaway: Annex A (Interior Design fees) replaces the old 1979 UAP Doc. 208.

questions.explanation: Annex 'A' of the 2010 SPP, which covers the Interior Design Fee Schedule, replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 208. This is a commonly tested distinction because the numbering shifted between the 1979 and 2010 series.

questions.text: SPP Document 208 (Architectural Design Competition) replaces which 1979 UAP document?

options.text: UAP Doc. 207
UAP Doc. 208
UAP Doc. 209
UAP Doc. 210

rationale.a: UAP Doc. 207 is incorrect. The old Doc. 207 was replaced by SPP Doc. 206 (Comprehensive Architectural Services).
rationale.b: UAP Doc. 208 is incorrect. The old Doc. 208 covered Interior Design fees and was replaced by Annex A, not SPP 208.
rationale.c: Correct. SPP 208 (Architectural Design Competition) replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 209. The numbering shifted in the 2010 revision.
rationale.d: UAP Doc. 210 did not exist in the 1979 series.
rationale.correct: SPP Doc. 208 (ADC) replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 209. This is a tricky numbering shift: the old Doc. 208 (Interior Design) became Annex A, while the old Doc. 209 (ADC) became SPP 208.
rationale.takeaway: SPP 208 (ADC) replaces old Doc. 209 — the numbering shifted when Interior Design moved to Annex A.

questions.explanation: SPP Doc. 208 (ADC) replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 209. This is a tricky numbering shift: the old Doc. 208 (Interior Design) became Annex A, while the old Doc. 209 (ADC) became SPP 208.

questions.text: What does the acronym SPPCC stand for under the UAP SPP framework?

options.text: Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost
Standards of Professional Practice Coordinating Committee
Standards of Professional Practice Compliance Council
Standards of Professional Practice Certification Commission

questions.rationale: Per SPP Document 202, SPPCC means Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost. The Architect prepares or updates the SPPCC during the design phases, but the SPP warns that such estimates have only a certain degree of accuracy because the Architect does not control labor, materials, and competitive bidding factors; the SPPCC is an estimate, not a guaranteed construction cost. 'Standards of Professional Practice Coordinating Committee' is a fabricated backronym and is an exam trap. Source: PRBoA SPP 202 (https://www.architectureboard.com.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/1.4-2010-SPP-for-PH-Architects.pdf).

questions.text: What are the requirements for a foreign architect to practice in the Philippines under the SPP?

options.text: Only a valid license from their home country, without needing local validation or oversight
A Temporary/Special Permit (TSP), DoLE certification, and collaboration with a local RLA
UAP membership and IAPOA endorsement, ensuring professional recognition within the local context
A reciprocity agreement between the Philippines and the foreign country, facilitating mutual practice rights

rationale.a: A home-country license alone is insufficient. Philippine law requires additional permits and local collaboration.
rationale.b: Correct. Foreign architects must obtain a Temporary/Special Permit (TSP) from the PRC, Department of Labor and Employment (DoLE) certification, and must collaborate with a local RLA.
rationale.c: UAP membership and IAPOA endorsement are not the statutory requirements. The legal framework is through PRC and DoLE.
rationale.d: While reciprocity agreements may exist, the SPP specifies the three-condition framework (TSP + DoLE + local RLA) regardless of reciprocity.
rationale.correct: Foreign architects must satisfy three conditions: (1) obtain a Temporary/Special Permit from PRC, (2) secure DoLE work certification, and (3) collaborate with a local Registered and Licensed Architect. This three-condition framework protects both professional standards and local practitioners.
rationale.takeaway: Foreign architects need TSP + DoLE permit + local RLA collaboration.

questions.explanation: Foreign architects must satisfy three conditions: (1) obtain a Temporary/Special Permit from PRC, (2) secure DoLE work certification, and (3) collaborate with a local Registered and Licensed Architect. This three-condition framework protects both professional standards and local practitioners.

questions.text: What registration requirements must an Architectural Firm satisfy to practice in the Philippines?

options.text: Registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) only, without needing additional certifications
Registration with either DTI (sole proprietorship) or SEC (partnership/corporation), plus PRC firm registration
Registration with the UAP and IAPOA only, focusing on professional affiliations
Registration with the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) only, applicable to small-scale firms

rationale.a: SEC registration alone is insufficient. Sole proprietorships register with DTI, and all firms need PRC registration.
rationale.b: Correct. Architectural firms must register with DTI (if sole proprietorship) or SEC (if partnership or corporation), and additionally secure PRC firm registration.
rationale.c: UAP/IAPOA membership is professionally important but not the legal registration requirement for firms.
rationale.d: DTI registration alone covers only sole proprietorships and omits the PRC requirement.
rationale.correct: An Architectural Firm must register with DTI (for sole proprietorship) or SEC (for partnership/corporation), and must also obtain PRC firm registration. This dual registration ensures both business legitimacy and professional compliance.
rationale.takeaway: Architectural firms need DTI or SEC registration PLUS PRC firm registration.

questions.explanation: An Architectural Firm must register with DTI (for sole proprietorship) or SEC (for partnership/corporation), and must also obtain PRC firm registration. This dual registration ensures both business legitimacy and professional compliance.

questions.text: How many SPP documents comprise the 2010 Standards of Professional Practice series, including Annex A?

options.text: 9 documents, excluding any annexes or supplementary materials
10 documents, which form the core of the series without additional annexes
10 documents plus Annex A (11 total)
12 documents, including all annexes and supplementary guidelines

rationale.a: 9 documents is incorrect. The series includes SPP 201 through 209 (9 numbered documents) plus Annex A.
rationale.b: 10 documents is incomplete. While there are 10 numbered items if you count SPP 200-209, the actual structure is SPP 201-209 plus Annex A.
rationale.c: Correct. The 2010 SPP series consists of 10 numbered documents (SPP 201 through 209, with 204 split into 204-A and 204-B) plus Annex A (Interior Design Fee Schedule), for a total of 11.
rationale.d: 12 documents is incorrect. There are only 11 total components in the SPP series.
rationale.correct: The 2010 SPP series comprises 10 numbered documents (SPP 201, 202, 203, 204-A, 204-B, 205, 206, 207, 208, 209) plus Annex A (Interior Design Fee Schedule), totaling 11 components.
rationale.takeaway: The SPP series has 10 numbered documents + Annex A = 11 total.

questions.explanation: The 2010 SPP series comprises 10 numbered documents (SPP 201, 202, 203, 204-A, 204-B, 205, 206, 207, 208, 209) plus Annex A (Interior Design Fee Schedule), totaling 11 components.

questions.text: Under the SPP, what defines a Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA)?

options.text: Any graduate of an architecture program, regardless of licensure status, which is a common misunderstanding
A natural person holding a valid PRC Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card
Any member of the United Architects of the Philippines, which is not a requirement for licensure
A person with a master's degree in architecture from a recognized institution, which is not a substitute for licensure

rationale.a: A graduate of architecture alone does not qualify as an RLA. Graduation is a prerequisite but does not confer the legal right to practice.
rationale.b: Correct. An RLA is specifically defined as a natural person (not a firm or corporation) who holds a valid Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card issued by the PRC.
rationale.c: UAP membership, while professionally important, is not the legal basis for RLA status. PRC registration is the statutory requirement.
rationale.d: A master's degree is not a requirement for RLA status. The requirement is passing the licensure examination and obtaining PRC registration.
rationale.correct: An RLA is a natural person who holds a valid PRC Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card. This definition emphasizes that only natural persons (not juridical entities) can be architects, and PRC registration is the sole legal basis.
rationale.takeaway: An RLA is a natural person with a valid PRC certificate — not a firm, not just a graduate.

questions.explanation: An RLA is a natural person who holds a valid PRC Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card. This definition emphasizes that only natural persons (not juridical entities) can be architects, and PRC registration is the sole legal basis.
